author: Vincent Chow
description:
Cooperation between the United States and China is required to manage the unprecedented societal impacts of rapidly advancing artificial intelligence (AI) technology, Bill Gates wrote in a new essay published on Wednesday.
The call to action comes as the billionaire philanthropist and tech titan warns that AI is ushering in “one of the most turbulent times in human history”, which could either become “the greatest equaliser ever invented, or the worst source of injustice”.
“[The] countries that...
title: Bill Gates warns of AI’s impact, urges the US and China to cooperate

author: William Zheng
description:
The South China Morning Post has launched a major data project diving into President Xi Jinping’s signature anti-graft campaign. In the third part of a series accompanying the data project, William Zheng looks at the relationship between rich regional resources and corruption.
Beneath the desolate Gobi Desert and sparsely populated mountains of China’s less developed regions lie abundant mineral resources, ranging from coal, the most basic fuel for China’s economy, to critical minerals needed...
title: Is ‘resource curse’ to blame in regions hit harder by Xi’s anti-corruption campaign?

author: Mark Magnier
description:
The Justice Department and the FBI said on Wednesday that they seized two Chinese state-sponsored online platforms that targeted US critical infrastructure and other critical networks, including Nasa, the Federal Reserve and the US Senate.
According to court documents, the seizures involved a group known as “QTFY”, operated by China-based Nanjing Xinjiuwei Network Technology Co, which created and ran the QScan and QTRouter sites.
“State-sponsored malicious hackers preying on America’s critical...
title: US seizes Chinese hacking platforms targeting Nasa, Fed and Senate

author: Igor Patrick
description:
Brazil has not answered two American proposals to formalise cooperation on critical minerals, a senior US diplomat said at Latin America’s largest mining fair, leaving Washington without a bilateral deal as it races to build rare earth supply chains outside China.
Matthew Lowe, economic counsellor at the US embassy in Brasilia, said Washington invited Brazil years ago to join the Minerals Security Partnership, a US-led grouping that coordinates investment in mineral supply chains, but never...
title: US critical minerals proposals to Brazil go unanswered as China looms

author: Vincent Chow,Lucy Quaggin
description:
The front page of the Danville Register & Bee, a local newspaper in southern Virginia with a circulation of fewer than 4,000, carried an unusual headline.
“LEADER: CHINA BEHIND THE MISCONCEPTIONS”, it read, above a photograph of two homes dwarfed by a data centre behind.
The leader in question was Vic Ingram, chair of the Danville-Pittsylvania Regional Industrial Facility Authority (RIFA), a local body jointly established by the city of Danville and neighbouring Pittsylvania County to promote...
title: In a small Virginia town, distrust of Big Tech hampers Trump’s AI push

author: Dewey Sim,Laura Zhou,Carol Yang
description:
Beijing has vowed to retaliate against Washington’s expanded Iran sanctions targeting Chinese entities, threatening a clash that could erode recent stability in the US-China relationship and become a new flashpoint weeks before President Xi Jinping visits the US, according to observers.
But they say that efforts on both sides, such as this week’s Track 1.5 dialogue, could serve as a check on tensions and allow each side to understand the other’s concerns.
The US on Monday announced fresh...
title: China vows payback for US Iran sanctions, testing stability ahead of Xi-Trump summit

author: Ling Xin
description:
China’s delay of a high-stakes mission to hunt for water ice near the moon’s south pole may slow its lunar ambitions, but is unlikely to change the bigger contest with the United States over who can build a lasting presence on the moon, according to space experts.
No reason was given when Chang’e-7 was postponed until next year, just hours before Sunday night’s scheduled lift-off, though a major tropical storm was approaching the launch site.
Chinese space authorities said only that the mission...
title: Could the delay to China’s moon mission ease pressure on Nasa?

author: Victoria Bela
description:
Scientists in China have created a self-exercising muscle graft that might allow bedridden people to gain the benefits of working out without any physical exertion.
With just an injection of muscle cells below the skin, the cells self-assembled into muscle grafts, which not only improved whole-body muscle mass in mice but also led to improvements in bone density, endurance, liver function and cognitive health.
The “myografts” could provide the health benefits of exercise to patients with...
title: No gym needed? Scientists in China develop self-exercising muscle grafts

author: Hao Nan
description:
Forty years ago, the Stockholm Document turned the political promise of the 1975 Helsinki Final Act into a more practical system of confidence-building. Amid the Cold War, Europe’s East and West did not disarm, abandon deterrence or begin to trust one another. Instead, they agreed that military competition could be made safer through prior notification, observation, information exchange and verification. The lesson was modest but durable: adversaries do not need trust to reduce uncertainty.
That...
title: The security-obsessed global economy needs its own Helsinki process

author: Khushboo Razdan,Cao Jiaxuan
description:
After two years of a cautious thaw, China and India are heading towards a pivotal test: can the relationship move beyond managed optics to meaningful engagement?
President Xi Jinping and Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi are expected to cross paths next week at the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) summit in Bishkek, Kyrgyzstan. Sources expect a short, tightly managed encounter on the sidelines of the August 31-September 1 summit that would set the stage for the main event – in...
title: China’s Xi Jinping expected to visit India after 7 years. What’s on the agenda?

author: Fan Chen,Xinlu Liang
description:
Rescue operations are under way after a landslide at the China-Nepal border engulfed a key border checkpoint, resulting in “major casualties”, according to Chinese state media.
The landslide began in Nepal at around 9am on Wednesday and also struck Tibet’s Gyirong county, which is under the administration of Shigatse city, according to Xinhua.
Footage circulating online showed the landslide engulfing the checkpoint in seconds as people on the ground fled, before mud and debris obscured the...
title: Landslide on China-Nepal border engulfs checkpoint, causing ‘major casualties’

author: Meredith Chen
description:
China has reminded its officials of their lifelong responsibility for serious environmental damage on their watch, tying green efforts more closely to performance assessments in the country’s push for higher-quality growth.
The conditions and potential disciplinary action were outlined in revised rules released on Tuesday by the Communist Party and the State Council, China’s cabinet.
Under the rules, officials will be held to account for serious environmental damage “regardless of whether they...
title: China makes officials liable for environmental damage for life

author: Khushboo Razdan,Cao Jiaxuan
description:
People in China reacted with frustration and disbelief after American consulates around the world began cancelling immigrant visa interviews – the latest setback for applicants waiting to enter the United States legally.
A post by an immigration agent on the Chinese social media platform RedNote claimed that the US consulate in Guangzhou had abruptly cancelled all immigrant visa interviews on Tuesday.
According to the agent, who declined to be named because they were not authorised to speak to...
title: Frustration in China as US freezes green card interviews worldwide, citing ‘training’

author: Brian Rhoads,Raymond Ma
description:
China warned of reprisals against possible United States sanctions as the Trump administration launched “economic D-Day” in a bid to isolate Iran following six months of military conflict.
“China will do everything necessary to firmly safeguard its rights and interests,” foreign ministry spokesman Lin Jian told reporters on Tuesday. Economic warfare would “only serve to fuel tensions and lead to risk spillover”, he said.
The US on Monday demanded countries take “immediate action” to cut economic...
title: US pulls China punches in Iran ‘economic D-Day’ sanctions

author: Albee Zhang
description:
China has tested a new variant of the YJ-18A anti-ship cruise missile bearing a black stealth coating, according to experts who say the advanced finish on the ship-launched missile will improve its penetration capability.
During a missile test in an unknown sea area, a missile was fired from a navy ship’s vertical launch system for an extreme-performance test of a new type of anti-ship missile, according to footage released by state broadcaster CCTV on Saturday that emphasised the missile’s...
title: Chinese navy fires new radar-absorbing YJ-18A anti-ship missile in sea trial: expert

author: David Gorombolyi
description:
As Washington increasingly turns away from the multilateral order it once helped build, Beijing is emerging as an advocate of international cooperation and rules-based stability. For some, the real surprise is that China’s rise is not challenging the world order but that its interests align with preserving it.
When I met Foreign Minister Wang Yi in the corridor of a congress centre in Myanmar, he had just finished addressing more than 50 foreign ministers, emphasising the need for a...
title: China’s multilateral pitch is finding an audience

author: SCMP
description:
We have put together stories from our coverage on science from the past two weeks to help you stay informed. If you would like to see more of our reporting, please consider subscribing.
1. Chinese team aims to put ‘smart’ diabetes probiotic on US shelves within 2 years
Chinese researchers have engineered a probiotic that could make diabetes care as simple as drinking a cup of yogurt or swallowing a capsule.
2. Chinese missile AI tracks F-22, F-35-like heat signatures with over 90% accuracy

The...
title: ‘Smart’ diabetes probiotic; Chinese missile AI with 90% accuracy: 7 science highlights

author: Orange Wang
description:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky has called on China to play a “strong diplomatic role” to help end the war between Russia and Ukraine, while sharing a letter from Chinese President Xi Jinping.
“We count on further cooperation and on China playing a strong diplomatic role in bringing Russia’s war against our country to an end,” the Ukrainian leader wrote on the social media platform X on Wednesday. “Peace can be our shared achievement.”
In his X posts on Monday, Zelensky attached copies of...
title: Zelensky urges China to use its diplomatic weight to end Russia’s war with Ukraine

author: Xinlu Liang
description:
Airports in China’s Zhejiang and Fujian provinces remained on high alert for potential delays and cancellations as Typhoon Saudel approached landfall on Wednesday, after multiple flights were cancelled in Taiwan and Hong Kong.
Saudel, which entered the East China Sea early on Wednesday morning, led to 16 cancelled flights at Taiwan’s Taoyuan International Airport. Affected carriers included Peach, China Airlines, EVA Air, Starlux and Thai Lion Air.
Hong Kong Airlines fully cancelled its...
title: China’s coastal regions on high alert as Typhoon Saudel cancels flights, ferries

author: Haining Gao
description:
The US Department of the Treasury launched targeted sanctions against some 24 entities based in mainland China or Hong Kong as part of its “Operation Economic Outcast” campaign against Iran and its enablers.


See below for the original announcement:

US Treasury sanctions by scmp
title: US Treasury sanctions on Iran’s trade partners

author: Holly Chik
description:
Long before the digital age, a Ming dynasty scholar made it his mission to map human knowledge from a Chinese perspective.
The result was an encyclopaedia spanning 127 volumes known as the Tushu Bian, or Compendium of Illustrations and Texts.
The work – published in 1613 – was compiled by Neo-Confucian scholar Zhang Huang and drew on more than 200 printed sources across several decades to document the concepts of heaven, Earth and humanity.
“His goal was to gather all the illustrations and texts...
title: Ming dynasty work shows how Chinese understood the world in the 1600s

author: Han Li
description:
South Carolina Senator Darline Graham won the Republican nomination in seeking a full term on Tuesday, overcoming a rocky moment in last week’s debate, when she struggled to answer questions about Taiwan and the South China Sea.
Graham, a political newcomer, was appointed to the seat in July following the unexpected death of her brother, Lindsey Graham, one of the Senate’s most senior and influential Republicans. Backed by US President Donald Trump, she was required to contest a special primary...
title: Trump pick Darline Graham wins election despite struggling over Taiwan question

author: Alyssa Chen
description:
A “widening” AI gap between advanced economies and developing countries has sparked calls to use the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation framework to develop an open, fairer and culturally sensitive governance system.
Although the technology is often hailed as a great leveller in an era of sluggish economic growth, a conference held in southern China last weekend heard that many Global South countries lacked the critical infrastructure and talent required to harness artificial intelligence...
title: Could Apec’s rules help close the growing AI gap between rich and poor?
